To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the smartphone is a contested technology that has been constructed in cultural discourse to be simultaneously a tool that should be integrated into everyday life and a tool that should not be integrated into everyday.

1) cultural narratives about the smartphone are contradictory; 2) these narratives are based on the same overarching cultural values; 3) these narratives create conflict for individuals who try to account for their actions with respect to the smartphone; and 4) this conflict creates instability for the cultural stories themselves.

(1) the smartphone is a site of cultural tension as people are encouraged to both integrate and dis-integrate it from everyday life, and (2) these contradictory stories call for the same values, but in different ways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how people talk about the smartphone, how these stories are told and how they are used to make sense of the world.
understanding and challenging the cultural narratives that shape how we think and talk about the smartphone.
how the smartphone has become a cultural object, and how this object is used in stories that shape and constrain individual actions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
smartphones are a complex technology that is both a source of conflict and tension in everyday life, as well as a source of instability in cultural discourse.
the smartphone is a powerful technology that can be used to connect and dis-connect, and that the stories we tell about it can have a profound effect on how it is used.
we need more nuanced and complex stories to better account for and design for the complex realities we live in.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified two common tropes in the stories of smartphones in American discourse, one calling for increased integration of smartphones and the other calling for disintegration from everyday life.
the smartphone, as a technology, has become a cultural artifact that people are trying to make sense of.
the smartphone is a technology that is both deeply valued and deeply problematic, and that the stories we tell about the smartphone are both compelling and simplistic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need more stories of technology that are complex, nuanced, and contradictory.
the smartphone is a contested technology that is not easily integrated into the fabric of everyday life.
stories of the smartphone are not just about the technology, but are about the values and tensions they evoke.
